title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
pitch: The whole species in one arc: cognitive revolution, agricultural trap, money and empire as shared fictions.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
pitch: Shifts the unit of selection from the organism to the gene, and invents the meme on the way out.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
pitch: Two systems, a catalogue of biases, and prospect theory — plus the replication caveats the book predates.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
author: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman
pitch: Programs as abstractions over process; builds an interpreter for its own language by chapter four.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
author: Jared Diamond
pitch: Geography, not race, as the engine of unequal development — and the serious objections to that thesis.

title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
pitch: Division of labour, the invisible hand, and how much of what Smith actually said gets misquoted.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
pitch: Not a prophecy but a mechanism: how language is engineered to make dissent unthinkable.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
pitch: Mendel to CRISPR, with the eugenics century placed where it belongs — in the middle, not the footnotes.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
author: Douglas Hofstadter
pitch: Self-reference as the common thread of incompleteness, fugue and mind. The hardest book on this shelf.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
pitch: Power described rather than justified, and the long argument over whether it is satire.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
pitch: Scale, from the cosmic calendar to the Library of Alexandria, and why the method matters more than the findings.

title: Prisoners of Geography
author: Tim Marshall
pitch: Ten maps that explain why states behave as they do — the North European Plain, warm-water ports, chokepoints.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
pitch: r > g, three centuries of tax records, and the data disputes that followed publication.

title: The Gulag Archipelago
author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
pitch: A camp system reconstructed from 227 testimonies, written where possession of the manuscript was a sentence.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
pitch: Affordances, signifiers, mapping and the Norman door: user error is usually design error.

title: Silent Spring
author: Rachel Carson
pitch: The book that created modern environmental regulation, and the industry campaign waged against it.

title: The Emperor of All Maladies
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
pitch: Cancer as a biography: radical surgery, the first chemotherapies, oncogenes, targeted therapy.

title: The Day of the Jackal
author: Frederick Forsyth
pitch: Procedural suspense with a known ending — the craft lesson in how tension survives a foregone conclusion.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
pitch: Relativity, quantum mechanics and black-hole thermodynamics without an equation, plus what has since changed.

title: The Mythical Man-Month
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.
pitch: Brooks's law, the second-system effect, conceptual integrity, and no silver bullet — fifty years and still load-bearing.

title: Why Nations Fail
author: Daron Acemoglu, James A. Robinson
pitch: Inclusive versus extractive institutions as the dividing line, argued from Nogales to the Congo.

title: The Sixth Extinction
author: Elizabeth Kolbert
pitch: Thirteen field trips, thirteen disappearing species, one mechanism: us moving things around.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven Levitt, Stephen Dubner
pitch: Incentives and natural experiments applied to sumo, crack and crime — including the abortion claim that drew fire.

title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
author: Richard Rhodes
pitch: Physics, politics and engineering braided from Szilard's 1933 insight to Hiroshima.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
pitch: Replication, partitioning, consistency models and consensus, with the failure modes stated honestly.

title: The Road to Serfdom
author: Friedrich Hayek
pitch: Central planning as a knowledge problem, written in wartime Britain and endlessly flattened since.

title: King Leopold's Ghost
author: Adam Hochschild
pitch: A privately owned colony, ten million dead, and the first modern human-rights campaign.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
pitch: HeLa cells, consent, and who owns tissue taken without asking.

title: The Spy Who Came In from the Cold
author: John le Carré
pitch: Espionage stripped of glamour: the operation whose real target is the man running it.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
pitch: One long argument, built from pigeons and barnacles, with the mechanism of heredity still missing.

title: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
author: Charles Petzold
pitch: From two flashlights and a wire to a working CPU, one relay at a time, nothing skipped.

title: Debt: The First 5,000 Years
author: David Graeber
pitch: Credit before coinage, the myth of barter, and debt as a moral instrument — plus where economists push back.

title: The Looming Tower
author: Lawrence Wright
pitch: Al-Qaeda's origins and the bureaucratic walls that kept US agencies from seeing 9/11 coming.

title: Entangled Life
author: Merlin Sheldrake
pitch: Fungi as networks, symbionts and solvents of the individual — mycorrhizae, lichens, yeasts, truffles.

title: The Black Swan
author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
pitch: Fat tails, silent evidence and the narrative fallacy: why the consequential event is the unmodelled one.

title: Orientalism
author: Edward Said
pitch: How scholarship constructed the East as an object of rule, and the discipline-wide fight it started.

title: The Soul of a New Machine
author: Tracy Kidder
pitch: One minicomputer built by an exhausted team in a basement: the best account of engineering as it is lived.

title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
author: Robert Sapolsky
pitch: One behaviour explained at widening timescales: seconds, hours, years, millennia.

title: Salt: A World History
author: Mark Kurlansky
pitch: A commodity history where taxes, trade routes, wars and preservation all run through one mineral.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
author: William L. Shirer
pitch: A correspondent's history from captured archives — monumental, partisan, and still the common starting point.

title: Algorithms to Live By
author: Brian Christian, Tom Griffiths
pitch: Optimal stopping, explore/exploit, caching and scheduling as advice for actual decisions.

title: An Immense World
author: Ed Yong
pitch: Umwelt by umwelt: echolocation, electroreception, magnetoreception — the senses we are not equipped to imagine.

title: The Big Short
author: Michael Lewis
pitch: Subprime, CDOs and synthetic CDOs explained through the handful of people who read the prospectuses.

title: The Information: A History, a Theory, a Flood
author: James Gleick
pitch: Talking drums to Shannon to entropy: information as a physical quantity with a measurable size.

title: Chaos: Making a New Science
author: James Gleick
pitch: Sensitive dependence, strange attractors and fractals, and how a field assembled itself from oddities.

title: Factfulness
author: Hans Rosling
pitch: Ten instincts that distort our picture of the world, each answered with a number you can check.

title: The Shock Doctrine
author: Naomi Klein
pitch: Crisis as the window for unpopular economic restructuring — a thesis worth reading with its critics beside it.

title: Thinking in Systems
author: Donella Meadows
pitch: Stocks, flows, feedback, delays and leverage points: the shortest route to systems literacy.

title: The Hot Zone
author: Richard Preston
pitch: Filoviruses and BSL-4 procedure as nonfiction horror — with notes on where it dramatises.

title: Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
author: Nick Bostrom
pitch: Orthogonality, instrumental convergence and the control problem, a decade before the current debate.

title: The Dawn of Everything
author: David Graeber, David Wengrow
pitch: Prehistory without the staircase: cities without kings, seasonal hierarchies, political experiment as the norm.

title: Superforecasting: The Art and Science of Prediction
author: Philip Tetlock, Dan Gardner
pitch: What the Good Judgment Project measured: scoring rules, Brier scores, and the habits of the people who win.
